source: Sample APA-7 Paper: Student Format for Undergraduate Students (Liberty University)

elements: Title of paper (bold, centered, title case)

line_spacing.extra_spacing: No extra lines or spacing between paragraphs
line_spacing.footnotes: Single-spaced when at bottom of page

general_formatting.spaces_after_punctuation: One space after closing punctuation (periods, etc.)
general_formatting.word_count_definition: Number of words in the body only; excludes title page, abstract, reference list, appendices, and supplemental resources

order: Body (title repeated on first line, bold, centered)

title_on_body_page.must_match: Title on the title page exactly

rules: Do not copy-paste sentences from the body

avoid: First person (I, me, we, us, our)
person.exceptions: Allowed when assignment instructions permit (e.g., personal reflections, life histories)

scholarly_writing_rules.purpose_of_research_paper: Compile, assimilate, and summarize others' scholarly research — not simply write a long essay of your own thoughts or string together direct quotes

acronyms.rule: Write out the full name the first time mentioned, followed by the acronym in brackets
acronyms.usage_threshold: Only abbreviate if the term appears 4+ times in the body
acronyms.under_threshold: Spell it out fully every time (no acronym)

purpose: Give proper credit to the originators of ideas
Allow readers to find and access your sources

narrative.description: Author named in the sentence text

parenthetical.description: Author and year in parentheses at end

page_and_paragraph_numbers.optional_for: Paraphrases (encouraged to help readers find content)
page_and_paragraph_numbers.paragraph_numbers_for: Online articles, webpages (when no page numbers exist)

frequency_per_paragraph.rule: Cite the source at least once per paragraph (first instance)
frequency_per_paragraph.condition: Reader must be able to discern which subsequent sentences derive from that source
frequency_per_paragraph.technique: Use pronouns (she, her, he, they) referring back to the cited author

omitting_year_in_narrative.rule: Year may be omitted in subsequent narrative citations within the same paragraph after the first mention

multiple_sources_in_one_citation.order: Alphabetical by first author's last name (matching reference list order)
multiple_sources_in_one_citation.prioritizing_sources: Place most prominent first, then add 'see also' before the rest
multiple_sources_in_one_citation.example: (Cable, 2013; see also Avramova, 2019; De Vries et al., 2013)

same_author_same_year.rule: Add lowercase letters after the year, starting with 'a'

three_or_more_authors.in_text_rule: First author's last name followed by 'et al.' (every time)
three_or_more_authors.et_al_format: Not italicized; 'al.' has a period, 'et' does not

paraphrasing.definition: Rephrasing another's idea in your own words, substantially different wording but same meaning
paraphrasing.not_acceptable: Changing only one word or rearranging the original order
paraphrasing.demonstrates: That you read, understood, and assimilated the research

short_quotes.format: Incorporated into the sentence in standard paragraph format
short_quotes.punctuation: Double quotation marks around the quote
short_quotes.period_placement: After the closing parenthesis of the citation
short_quotes.mid_sentence_quote: Add parenthetical citation immediately after the closing quote mark

block_quotes.format: Indented 0.5 inch from left margin, no quotation marks
block_quotes.period_placement: Before the parenthetical page citation (opposite of short quotes)
block_quotes.introduction: Preferred to introduce with source and year, then lead into the quote

quotes_within_quotes.in_block_quotes: Use double quotation marks (since no outer quotes exist)

quotes.when_to_use: Only when the original text cannot be said as well in your own words, or changing the wording would alter the author's meaning

heading_levels.do_not_capitalize: Articles (a, an, the) unless they begin a title or follow a colon

level_1.content_position: New paragraph on the next line

level_2.content_position: New paragraph on the next line

level_3.content_position: New paragraph on the next line

level_4.format: Indented 0.5 inch, bold, title case, period at end
level_4.content_position: Begins on the same line after the period

level_5.format: Indented 0.5 inch, bold, italic, title case, period at end
level_5.content_position: Begins on the same line after the period

usage_rules: Must use two or more of each subheading level used
Not every paper needs every level
Start with Level 1 and work down
Most student papers use only Levels 1 and 2

numbers.exceptions: Ages are always numerical (see APA section 6.32)
numbers.beginning_a_sentence: Always write out the number in word format

titles_of_works_in_text.general_guidance: Naming source titles in the body is strongly discouraged; citing author and year is sufficient

primary_vs_secondary_sources.primary_source: The one that first published the content
primary_vs_secondary_sources.secondary_source: The one that quotes another previously published source
primary_vs_secondary_sources.preferred_approach: Find, read, and cite the original (primary) source whenever possible

when_citing_secondary.in_text_format: Use 'as cited in' to indicate the secondary source
when_citing_secondary.example: James Morgan hinted that 'goat milk makes the best ice cream' (as cited in Alone, 2008, p. 117)
when_citing_secondary.reference_list: Only list the secondary source (the one you actually read)

personal_communications.example_narrative: L. Applebaum advised him to dip pretzel rolls in cheese fondue (personal communication, July 13, 2015)

bible_citations.author_position: Bible version name (e.g., King James Bible)

class_lectures_and_powerpoints.powerpoint_citation: Include slide number instead of page number

liberty_university_lectures.format: Video lecture reference with URL if available
liberty_university_lectures.author: Presenter name(s); if unknown, use 'Liberty University'
include: Enough detail to identify within the course

dictionary_entries.format: Same as chapters in an edited book
dictionary_entries.author: Individual, group, or corporate author of the dictionary

reference_list.heading: Centered, bold ('References' or 'Reference' for one source)

formatting.hanging_indent: Second and subsequent lines indented 0.5 inch
formatting.order: Alphabetical by first author's last name
formatting.spacing: Double-spaced, no extra spacing between entries

number_of_authors.up_to_20: List all authors with last names and initials
number_of_authors.21_or_more: List first 19 authors, then ellipsis (...), then last author

reference_list.entry_structure: Author(s), Year of publication, Title of resource, Location details (journal/volume/issue/pages, publisher, or URL)
exceptions: Primary sources cited via secondary sources (only list the secondary)

urls.consistency: Use same style throughout (blue-underlined or plain black text)
urls.break_long_urls: Soft returns (Shift+Enter) at forward slashes, periods, or underscores

retrieved_from.use_when: Content may have changed (dictionary entries, social media, no known publication date)

electronic_sources.publication_dates_online: Full date in year, month day format (e.g., 2020, October 8)

miscellaneous_reference_rules.publisher_location: Omitted (no city/state), except for conference presentations
miscellaneous_reference_rules.issue_numbers: Required for all journal articles that have them
miscellaneous_reference_rules.multiple_publishers: List all, separated by semicolons, in order listed

tables_and_figures.note: APA-7 dedicates an entire 55-page chapter to tables and figures; rules are complex

appendices.label: 'Appendix' (singular) at top of page, centered, bold
appendices.descriptive_title: Centered, bold, title case, beneath the label
appendices.must_be_referenced: Callout in the body text (e.g., 'see Appendix')

annotated_bibliographies.purpose: Critique resources and rationalize relevance to the paper's focus

self_plagiarism.apa_allows: Limited duplication of own prior work without quotation marks when material is limited in scope
self_plagiarism.apa_prohibits: Quotation marks or block quote formatting around own duplicated material
self_plagiarism.liberty_university_rule: Expressly forbids reusing significant portions of a prior paper in a subsequent course
self_plagiarism.if_incorporating_brief_excerpts: Disclose with 'I have previously discussed', cite the prior paper, and include a reference entry

final_formatting_checklist: Select all text (Ctrl+A) and verify correct font/size
Set paragraph spacing 'before' and 'after' to 0 pt
Title page spacing is handled by the template
